knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 3.1.2
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly describes maximum-likelihood estimation and how it differs from method of moments?
knowledge_checks.body: Select the statement that names the MLE move and contrasts it with MoM.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: MLE maximises the model likelihood (or log-likelihood). MoM matches moments. The two constructions are different even when numerical answers sometimes coincide. MSE comparison is a property criterion, not the MLE definition.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Maximise the likelihood (or log-likelihood); MoM matches moments instead.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Collapsing MoM into MLE, or defining MLE as an MSE-optimality rule.

choices.label: Choose the parameter value that maximises the likelihood (equivalently the log-likelihood under regularity). Method of moments instead equates sample moments to population moments.
Maximum likelihood always equates the first sample moment to the first population moment; that is what 'likelihood' means here.
Once a method-of-moments estimator exists, the maximum-likelihood estimator is the same object by definition.
Maximum likelihood means choosing the parameter that minimises mean square error among all unbiased estimators.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: Exponential rate MLE
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Four independent claim settlement delays (months) are modelled as Exponential with rate λ (pdf f(x) = λ e^{−λx} for x > 0): 2, 3, 1, 4. Enter the maximum-likelihood estimate of λ.
knowledge_checks.body: Compute λ̂_MLE from the four observations.
hints: Form ℓ(λ) = n ln λ − λ Σxᵢ, then solve the score equation.
For the rate parametrisation, λ̂ = n / Σxᵢ, not the sample mean.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Σxᵢ = 2+3+1+4 = 10 and n = 4, so λ̂_MLE = n/Σxᵢ = 4/10 = 0.4 per month. The sample mean x̄ = 2.5 is the MLE of the mean, not of the rate.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Reporting x̄ = 2.5 (or Σxᵢ/n) when the question asks for the rate λ̂ = n/Σxᵢ = 0.4.
success_criteria: Uses n/Σxᵢ for the rate, not the sample mean.

worked_example.title: MLE for Exponential claim waiting times
worked_example.problem_statement: Four independent claim settlement delays (months) are modelled as Exponential with rate λ (pdf f(x) = λ e^{−λx} for x > 0): 2, 3, 1, 4. Find the maximum-likelihood estimate of λ.
worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Write the log-likelihood ℓ(λ) before differentiating.

steps.label: Form the likelihood and log-likelihood
steps.attempt_cue: Write L(λ) = λⁿ exp(−λ Σxᵢ) and ℓ(λ) = n ln λ − λ Σxᵢ.
steps.explanation: Independence multiplies the densities. The log turns the product into a sum that is easy to differentiate.

steps.label: Differentiate and solve the score equation
steps.attempt_cue: Set dℓ/dλ = 0 and solve for λ.
steps.explanation: The MLE solves the score equation. For Exponential rate, this yields λ̂ = n / Σxᵢ = 1/x̄.

steps.label: Confirm it is a maximum
steps.attempt_cue: Check the second derivative sign at λ̂.
steps.explanation: d²ℓ/dλ² = −n/λ² < 0 for λ > 0, so the critical point is a maximum.

worked_example.common_pitfall: Reporting the MLE of the mean μ̂ = x̄ = 2.5 when the question asked for the rate λ, or writing λ̂ = Σxᵢ/n = 2.5 instead of n/Σxᵢ.
